summary: Yoshio Kawakatsu was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and under Paul Demiéville (~1956–1958), later serving as an assistant librarian at Kyoto University (~1952–1984).
Yoshio Takeuchi worked in sinology and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University from ~1907 to 1910, he held a post at Tohoku University from ~1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Otani, EPHE, and Paris Diderot under Ariane Macdonald and Rolf A. Stein, he held appointments at CNRS, the National Library of Bhutan, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology scholar. He studied at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Toyo University, later holding professorial posts at Toyo, the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of Chicago.

Yoshitaka Iriya was a sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, Nagoya University, Kyoto Sangyo University, Hanazono University, and the University of Hamburg.
Yoshitoyo Ohara works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He held attested posts at Kyoto University in 2006 and Kyoto National Museum in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard under scholars including Daniel H. H. Ingalls and John B. Carman, and later served as professor and dean at Tenri University (~1985–2017).
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2006) and as a specially appointed lecturer (attested 2015).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe earned his doctorate at Tohoku University (~1970–1975) and served there as an assistant (1975–2012) and senior research fellow (2018). He held visiting positions at UC Berkeley, JAIST, and universities in China and Australia.

Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He served as a professor at Rissho University (~1961–1987) and director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1975–1986).

Youlan Feng was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, and Columbia University. He held academic posts at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Youru Wang works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, later holding posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.
Youwei Kang was a scholar in philosophy, sinology, and history/archaeology. He founded Wanmu Caotang in 1890, held a post there from ~1891 to 1898, and taught Qichao Liang.

Yozo Taniyama is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996). He held posts at Tohoku University, International Buddhist University, St. Thomas University (Japan), and Sophia University.
Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She pursued master's studies at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, undertook doctoral supervision under Natasha Heller, and studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-guang Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Samten, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).

Yu-kwan Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and McMaster University under Yun-hua Jan, Graeme MacQueen, and Koichi Shinohara, later holding posts at Hong Kong Baptist University and National Central University.
Yu-min Lee works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed graduate study under John C. Huntington and held an attested post as professor at National Taiwan University in 2002.
Yuan Ren is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who completed a PhD at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 1998).
